definitions.explanation: A ceremony held at the beginning of the school year to welcome new students.

examples.japanese: {入学式|にゅうがくしき}は4{月|がつ}に{行|おこな}われる。
examples.english: The entrance ceremony is held in April.

examples.japanese: {入学式|にゅうがくしき}に{親|おや}も{出席|しゅっせき}する。
examples.english: Parents also attend the entrance ceremony.

examples.japanese: {大学|だいがく}の{入学式|にゅうがくしき}はとても{盛大|せいだい}だった。
examples.english: The university entrance ceremony was very grand.

notes:
A formal ceremony welcoming new students at the start of the school year. Held at all levels — elementary through university.

TIMING:
Held in April at the start of the Japanese school year. {桜|さくら} (cherry blossoms) are iconic symbols of this event.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {入学式|にゅうがくしき}に{出席|しゅっせき}する: to attend an entrance ceremony
- {入学式|にゅうがくしき}を{行|おこな}う: to hold an entrance ceremony

CULTURAL NOTE:
Parents typically attend. Students wear {制服|せいふく} (school uniforms) or formal attire. At elementary schools, first-graders often carry their new ランドセル (school backpacks). The ceremony includes speeches from the principal and sometimes older students.

CONTRAST:
- {卒業式|そつぎょうしき}: graduation ceremony (held in March)
- {始業式|しぎょうしき}: opening ceremony of a new term (less formal)
